56368-alhalla-or-the-lord-of-talladega-a.description: A book by Henry Rowe Colcraft.. he imagination, the image of the lithe Indian, with his Robin Hood arms and his picturesque costume. The policy which an enlightened government and people ought to pursue towards them, at all times, is a question that chiefly concerns the statesman and the philanthropist.

arxiv-1811-02133.title: On the Termination Problem for Probabilistic Higher-Order Recursive Programs
arxiv-1811-02133.creator: Naoki Kobayashi \rsuper a, Ugo Dal Lago \rsuper b, Charles Grellois \rsuper c
arxiv-1811-02133.description: Abstract . In the last two decades, there has been much progress on model checking of both probabilistic systems and higher-order programs. In spite of the emergence of higher-order probabilistic programming languages, not much has been done to combine those two approaches.

arxiv-2111-07750.title: Observation of spin-dependent dual ferromagnetism in perovskite ruthenates
arxiv-2111-07750.creator: Sungsoo Hahn, Byungmin Sohn, Minjae Kim, Jeong Rae Kim, Soonsang Huh, Younsik Kim, Wonshik Kyung, Minsoo Kim, Donghan Kim, Youngdo Kim, Tae Won Noh, Ji Hoon Shim, Changyoung Kim
arxiv-2111-07750.description: Abstract We performed in-situ angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-resolved ARPES (SARPES) experiments to investigate the relationship between electronic band structures and ferromagnetism in SrRuO 3 (SRO) thin films. Our high quality ARPES and SARPES results show clear spin-lifted band structures.

arxiv-2204-04840.title: Nonparametric Bayes Differential Analysis of Multigroup DNA Methylation Data
arxiv-2204-04840.creator: Chiyu Gu
arxiv-2204-04840.description: Abstract DNA methylation datasets in cancer studies are comprised of measurements on a large number of genomic locations called cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites with complex correlation structures. A fundamental goal of these studies is the development of statistical techniques that can identify disease genomic signatures across multiple patient groups defined by different experimental or biological conditions.

arxiv-2206-11682.title: EFFGAN: Ensembles of fine-tuned federated GANs
arxiv-2206-11682.creator: 1 st Ebba Ekblom, 2 nd Edvin Listo Zec, 3 rd Olof Mogren
arxiv-2206-11682.description: Abstract Decentralized machine learning tackles the problem of learning useful models when data is distributed among several clients. The most prevalent decentralized setting today is federated learning (FL), where a central server orchestrates the learning among clients. In this work, we contribute to the relatively understudied sub-field of generative modelling in the FL framework.

arxiv-2306-14464.title: Quantum fluctuations lead to glassy electron dynamics in the good metal regime of electron doped KTaO 3
arxiv-2306-14464.creator: Shashank Kumar Ojha, Sankalpa Hazra, Surajit Bera, Sanat Kumar Gogoi, Prithwijit Mandal, Jyotirmay Maity, A. Gloskovskii, C. Schlueter, Smarajit Karmakar, Manish Jain, Sumilan Banerjee, Venkatraman Gopalan, Srimanta Middey
arxiv-2306-14464.description: Abstract Abstract: One of the central challenges in condensed matter physics is to comprehend systems that have strong disorder and strong interactions. In the strongly localized regime, their subtle competition leads to glassy electron dynamics which ceases to exist well before the insulator-to-metal transition is approached as a function of doping.

arxiv-2311-14172.title: Metrological Advantages in Seeded and Lossy Nonlinear Interferometers
arxiv-2311-14172.creator: Jasper Kranias, Guillaume Thekkadath, Khabat Heshami, Aaron Z. Goldberg
arxiv-2311-14172.description: Abstract The quantum Fisher information (QFI) bounds the sensitivity of a quantum measurement, heralding the conditions for quantum advantages when compared with classical strategies. Here, we calculate analytical expressions for the QFI of nonlinear interferometers under lossy conditions and with coherent-state seeding.

arxiv-2401-09879.title: One-loop partition functions in T ​ T ¯ T\overline{T} -deformed AdS 3
arxiv-2401-09879.description: Abstract We study the geometry of T ​ T ¯ T\bar{T} -deformed BTZ black hole and find it can be regarded as a quotient of hyperbolic space. We then consider the massive scalar field propagating in the T ​ T ¯ T\bar{T} -deformed BTZ black hole background.

arxiv-2507-21283.title: Topological indicators for systems with open boundaries: Application to the Kitaev wire
arxiv-2507-21283.creator: Balázs Hetényi 1,2 , András Lászlóffy 1 , Karlo Penc 1 , and Balázs Újfalussy 1
arxiv-2507-21283.description: Abstract To clarify the relationship between edge electronic states in open-boundary crystalline systems and their corresponding bulk electronic structure, Alase et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 076804 (2016)] have recently generalized Bloch’s theorem to lattice models with broken translational symmetry. Their formalism provides a bulk-boundary correspondence indicator, D, sensitive directly to the localization of edge states.

arxiv-2509-13778.title: Imputation-Powered Inference
arxiv-2509-13778.creator: Sarah Zhao, Emmanuel Candès
arxiv-2509-13778.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sarah Zhao, Emmanuel Candès. Modern multi-modal and multi-site data frequently suffer from blockwise missingness, where subsets of features are missing for groups of individuals, creating complex patterns that challenge standard inference methods. Existing approaches have critical limitations: complete-case analysis discards informative data and is potentially biased; doubly robust estimators for non-monotone missingness—where the missingness patterns are not nested subsets of one another—can be theoretically efficient but lack closed-form solutions and often fail to scale; and blackbox imputation can leverage partially observed data to improve

plos-pone-0008864.description: PLOS ONE research article. Androgen ablation therapy is currently the primary treatment for metastatic prostate cancer. Unfortunately, in nearly all cases, androgen ablation fails to permanently arrest cancer progression. As androgens like testosterone are withdrawn, prostate cancer cells lose their androg

pmc-11446148.title: Explore genetic susceptibility association between viral infections and Guillain-Barré syndrome risk using two-sample Mendelian randomization
pmc-11446148.creator: Qing-Xiang Kong, Zhao-Kun Gao, Yan Liu, Lu-Lu Jiang, Yuan-Jie Liu, Zhi-Yun Lian
pmc-11446148.description: BackgroundNumerous observational studies have indicated that patients with Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) frequently had infections with various pathogens before the onset of the disease, particularly several viral infections. Some of these infections are linked to specific clinical and immunological subgroups of GBS, suggesting a potential correlation between viral infections and the development of GBS.

pmc-12554147.title: Unlocking private finance for nature: Addressing barriers and reframing risk-return dynamics
pmc-12554147.creator: Hassan Aftab Sheikh, Divya Narain, Clint Bartlett, Christophe Christiaen
pmc-12554147.description: SummaryPublic finance alone is insufficient to meet the scale of investment required for nature protection, restoration, and sustainable management. Mobilizing private capital is therefore essential, yet most nature-related projects are perceived as unbankable. They sit at the frontier of bankability: nascent and unproven initiatives that lack historical track records, face high execution risks, and generate uncertain or delayed revenues.

pmc-12592093.title: Signet‐Ring Cell Type Adenocarcinoma of the Urachus: A Rare Case
pmc-12592093.creator: Samin Khannejad, Sevim Soleimani, Hamed Rajaii, Ali Goudarzi Karim
pmc-12592093.description: Urachal adenocarcinoma is a rare subset of bladder cancer originating from the urachus. We present a case of a 62‐year‐old woman with a 2‐year history of persistent dysuria, urinary frequency, and urgency. On physical examination, a firm, non‐tender suprapubic mass was detected. Cystoscopy was performed and a bladder mass was detected.

pmc-12991364.title: Impacts of parental age and inbreeding on fitness in a wild insect
pmc-12991364.creator: Tom Tregenza, Rolando Rodríguez-Muñoz, Alfredo F. Ojanguren, Paul Hopwood, Jelle J. Boonekamp, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia, Ines Alvarez-Garcia
pmc-12991364.description: Parental age and inbreeding have both been shown to have substantial fitness effects in laboratory experiments and in observations of wild animals. These demographic effects are likely to be strongly impacted by habitat fragmentation and warming temperatures, so understanding them is a priority. In insects and other ectotherms, some processes implicated in senescence are dependent on temperature.

pmc-13109038.title: Evaluation of Porous Media Properties for the Performance of Sulfur‐Depolarized Electrolysis
pmc-13109038.creator: Lukas Roessler Escudero, Ádám Székeli, Viktor Hacker, Merit Bodner
pmc-13109038.description: Sulfur‐depolarized electrolysis (SDE) is an interesting alternative for H2 production. Lower operational voltage (<1.2 V) and a valuable by‐product offer an opportunity for economically competitive H2 production in sectors where traditional processes are not feasible or competitive. However, given its incipient state in development, several questions are yet to be answered to achieve stable, competitive operation.

pmc-13212794.title: Sex differences in the long-term tolerability of BNT162b2 in children and adolescents
pmc-13212794.creator: Jeanne Moor, Vivien Grieshaber, Nicole Toepfner, Sarah Holzwarth, Matthias B. Moor, Karolina Kublickiene, Christoph Strumann, Cho-Ming Chao
pmc-13212794.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSex differences exist not only in the efficacy but also in adverse event rates of many vaccines. Here we compared the sex differences in the tolerability of BNT162b2 in children younger than 18 years in Germany.MethodsA post-hoc analysis of retrospectively collected tolerability data, collected through an authentication-based survey of legal guardians of children vaccinated with BNT162b2 under the age of 18 years (CoVacU18-study).

pmc-13414853.title: The Central Role of the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α Signaling Axis in Skeletal Muscle Physiology and Pathology and Its Targeted Therapeutic Strategies
pmc-13414853.creator: Jie Wang, Jiayi Gu, Xia Li, Hualin Sun, Xiaoming Yang
pmc-13414853.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Considered by some to be the largest metabolic organ of the body, the functional integrity of skeletal muscle is highly dependent on its exceptional plasticity, which is primarily governed by mitochondrial quality control. The signaling axis composed of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α) serves as a critical hub that senses cellular energy status, coordinates mitochondrial biogenesis, regulates muscle fiber type switching, and maintains protein homeostasis.

pmc-13506325.title: Cancer is an RNA disease: DNA is not destiny, RNA determines leukemia fate
pmc-13506325.creator: Inge van der Werf, Catriona Helen Macleod Jamieson
pmc-13506325.description: t in haematological abnormalities or progress to leukaemia. Also, the same variant can be associated with different cancer phenotypes and trajectories. Further, there is a distinct peak in leukemia incidence during infancy despite the limited time to acquire somatic pathogenic variants. These data suggest somatic variants alone do not fully explain leukemia development.

pmc-13634163.title: Comparative Cost Modeling of Out-of-Pocket Costs for External Beam Radiation Therapy Versus Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy in Metastatic Spine Cancer
pmc-13634163.creator: Victoria Wu, Martha Khlopin, Shearwood McClelland III
pmc-13634163.description: Purpose: The choice between stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) and external beam radiation therapy (EBRT) for spine metastases depends on several factors: tumor size, tumor location, patient health, prognosis, other treatments (i.e., surgery, minimally invasive procedures, systemic therapy, and supportive care), and treatment goals. Limited evidence exists on insurance's influence on out-of-pocket (OOP) expenses across radiation modalities.
